texto:
Value-based bidding is a family of automated bid strategies that set a price for each ad auction according to how much revenue, profit or other value a conversion is expected to bring, rather than simply how likely a conversion is. It exists because conversions are not equal. A retailer selling 40 dollar phone cases and 900 dollar laptops gains little from a system that counts both orders as "one conversion". Value-based bidding asks the advertiser to attach a number to each outcome and then tells the platform to chase the larger numbers.
Google describes it as a subset of Smart Bidding that "optimizes for conversion value rather than conversion volume", according to its Search and Shopping help page. Meta, TikTok and Microsoft Advertising run equivalents.
How the bid is calculated
Every value-based system makes two predictions at auction time: the probability of a conversion and the value it is likely to carry. Their product is the auction's expected value, and the strategy decides how much of it to spend.
A worked example shows the arithmetic. Suppose a click has a predicted conversion rate of 2% and a predicted order value of 150 dollars. Expected value is 3 dollars. Under a Target ROAS (return on ad spend) of 500%, meaning 5 dollars of value for every dollar spent, the implied bid is 3 divided by 5, or 60 cents. A second click with the same conversion probability but a predicted basket of 600 dollars justifies a bid of 2.40 dollars. Target CPA (cost per acquisition) would have bid the same on both.
Google offers two strategies built on this logic. Maximize conversion value spends the daily budget to generate as much value as possible "without any constraints". Target ROAS pursues maximum value while holding to a set efficiency ratio. A lower target makes the strategy "more competitive in auctions", while a higher one may "restrict the number of auctions" entered, according to Google. Since June 2026 the second option has been labelled simply "Target ROAS" again, after five years presented as an optional target inside Maximize conversion value. Google said the algorithm itself did not change. The API types are TARGET_ROAS
and MAXIMIZE_CONVERSION_VALUE
.
Meta's version sits on the ad set. Setting optimization_goal
to VALUE
makes "Highest Value" the bid strategy in Ads Manager, according to Meta's Marketing API documentation. The constrained variant, LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS
, requires a roas_average_floor
expressed as an integer scaled 10,000 times: 15000 means a minimum ROAS of 1.5, within a valid range of 100 to 10,000,000. TikTok's Value-based Optimization (VBO) for web offers the same pair, Highest Value or Minimum ROAS, according to TikTok's help centre.
Where the value comes from
The bid is only as good as the value fed into it.
Transaction values are passed in the conversion tag or pixel at the moment of purchase. Google requires "two or more unique values" before value bidding makes sense, either dynamic values on a single goal or static values spread across different goals.
Offline and proxy values arrive later. Lead-generation businesses rarely know revenue at the moment of a form fill, so Google's best-practice page suggests lead scores, values tied to lead-form answers, profit margins or predicted lifetime value, and recommends uploading data daily through enhanced conversions for leads or Google Ads Data Manager. Google product manager Carlo Buchmann told the Ads Decoded series in March 2026 that the aim is the lowest conversion action in the journey "that will have volume and is a high-quality indicator of value".
Adjusted values are applied by the platform on the advertiser's instruction. Conversion value rules on Google and value rules on Meta raise or lower values by audience, location or device. Customer lifecycle goals add value for new or lapsed customers. On October 22, 2026, Google moved percentage multipliers for new customer values out of beta, allowing uplifts from 1.1x to 5x across Search, Shopping, Performance Max and Demand Gen. At 1.2x, a 100 dollar first purchase counts as 120 dollars.
Lifetime value (LTV) inputs are the most ambitious form. The advertiser passes a predicted lifetime figure, or a premium for new buyers, so the system bids more for customers expected to return. Google's lifecycle goals, expanded on April 8, 2025, include a Performance Max mode for high-value new customers that works only with value-based bidding.
Data thresholds and operating rules
Value bidding needs more data than count bidding because it learns two predictions. Google's help page recommends at least 15 conversions in the last 30 days for Target ROAS, conversion delays under seven days, and three weeks or one to two conversion cycles of value uploads before switching. A separate best-practice page says four weeks or three cycles. Demand Gen is stricter: 50 conversions with value in 35 days at campaign level, including 10 in the last seven, plus 100 across the account, with no bid or creative changes for 14 days after launch.
Evaluation windows differ again. Google's June 2026 guidance says Target ROAS should be judged over at least 50 conversions with "meaningful, varied conversion values", against 30 for Target CPA. Ginny Marvin, Google's Ads Liaison, gave a 50-conversion or one-month rule for lead generation in August 2024, warning that tight budgets or cost-per-click caps hold the system back.
Origins and evolution
The lineage starts in search. Google's Conversion Optimizer, announced on September 24, 2007, automated bids toward a cost per acquisition. Value entered on October 3, 2013, when Wilfred Yeung, a product manager for bidding in AdWords, announced a Target ROAS flexible bid strategy. A return of 7 dollars per dollar was entered as 700%. "Your target ROAS represents how much revenue you want to earn for each dollar you spend on AdWords," Yeung wrote, according to the AdWords blog.
Google placed value and count strategies under the Smart Bidding name in July 2016 and added Maximize conversion value, with a preview of conversion value rules, in May 2019. In April 2021 Target ROAS was folded into Maximize conversion value as an optional target, a structure reversed in June 2026.
Social platforms followed the same path. Facebook announced Value Optimization on June 12, 2017, estimating how much a person would spend over seven days from pixel data and adjusting bids accordingly, according to Social Samosa. Minimum ROAS bidding followed in August 2018. On June 4, 2025, Meta extended value optimisation to non-purchase events and began testing profit-based ROAS through the Conversions API, with an average 12% ROAS improvement claimed from its own tests.
Microsoft Advertising extended conversion value bidding to standard search and shopping campaigns in April 2024, and from August 4, 2025 stopped offering Target ROAS as a standalone strategy for new campaigns, the opposite direction to Google a year later.
Why it matters
For advertisers, value-based bidding moves the optimisation target closer to the profit and loss account. It also moves responsibility: the platform optimises whatever number it receives. Kristina Park, a Google Ads product manager for budgets and bidding, said in the March 2026 Ads Decoded episode that "a lot of businesses actually do care about conversion value" but find it "more difficult for them to pass that back into Google Ads". Her biggest named pitfall was values that do not reflect business goals, where a campaign hits its ROAS target while the business does not.
Margin is the obvious gap. A revenue-based target treats a 30 dollar product with thin margin as more valuable than a 20 dollar product with a fat one. Google's cost of goods sold (COGS) profit optimisation and Meta's profit-based ROAS test both target it.
Limitations and disputes
Inflated values draw most complaints. When Google tested a tool in February 2026 that converts a new-customer ROAS target into a suggested account-wide value, practitioners objected that it inflates the conversion value column. Branden Antolick stopped using it for that reason; Andrew Lolk of Savvy Revenue argued for a lower ROAS target on new customers instead of added value. Meta's value rules drew similar criticism.
Target behaviour is contested too. Google's change of August 17, 2026 pulls budget-limited Target CPA and Target ROAS campaigns that beat their targets back toward them. A PPC Land analysis described one Shopping campaign with a 300% target that had been returning 3,000% to 4,000% and lost sales after the change, arguing the target becomes a floor on the platform's behalf. Google says targets should mean what they say.
Structural limits remain. Attributed value is not caused value, so a system rewarded for platform-reported revenue can bid heavily on customers who would have bought anyway. Long sales cycles starve the model of signal. Reporting also diverges: Google added an "original conversion value" column in November 2025 to show values before rules and adjustments.
What it is not
Smart Bidding is the wider Google family of auction-time automated strategies. Value-based bidding is the subset that optimises toward value; Maximize conversions and Target CPA are the count-based members.
Target CPA bids to acquire conversions at an average cost, treating each conversion as equal. Google's own guidance points advertisers who "care more about driving conversion volume" to it instead.
Value-based pricing is a pricing strategy for products, setting a price according to what customers perceive a product is worth rather than its cost. It concerns what a business charges, not what it pays for ads.
Recent developments
Google relabelled Target ROAS in June 2026, then applied the August 17 target change across five campaign types, with rollout complete by August 27. On October 22, 2026, Google made percentage multipliers for new customer value generally available and announced high value mode for Shopping, while PPC Land noted that Google had not said whether multipliers apply in the auction, to reported value, or both. As of October 2026, Meta's profit-based ROAS remains in testing.

- July 2016: Google groups automated conversion strategies under the Smart Bidding name

- August 2018: Facebook announces Minimum ROAS bidding
- May 2019: Google launches Maximize conversion value and previews conversion value rules
- April 2021: Google folds Target ROAS into Maximize conversion value as an optional target
- April 2024: Microsoft Advertising extends conversion value bidding to standard search and shopping campaigns
- August 9, 2024: Ginny Marvin closes Google's five-part series on value-based bidding for lead generation
- April 8, 2025: Google expands customer lifecycle goals, including a value-only High Value New Customer mode
- June 4, 2025: Meta extends value optimisation to non-purchase events and tests profit-based ROAS
- June 2025: Google sets value-based bidding thresholds for Demand Gen at 50 valued conversions in 35 days
- August 4, 2025: Microsoft stops offering standalone Target ROAS for new campaigns
- November 2025: Google adds an original conversion value column
- February 13, 2026: Google tests a tool deriving new-customer values from a ROAS target
- June 2026: Google relabels "Maximize conversion value with a Target ROAS" as "Target ROAS"
- August 17, 2026: Google's target change for budget-limited campaigns takes effect
- October 22, 2026: Google makes 1.1x to 5x new customer value multipliers generally available

Summary
Who: Google Ads, Meta, Microsoft Advertising and TikTok operate value-based bidding systems; advertisers supply the conversion values, and agencies and practitioners debate how those values should be set.
What: Automated bid strategies, such as Target ROAS, Maximize conversion value, Highest Value and Minimum ROAS, that price each auction on predicted conversion value rather than conversion count.
When: Google introduced Target ROAS on October 3, 2013, and Facebook launched Value Optimization in June 2017; the latest changes include Google's June 2026 relabelling, its August 17, 2026 target change and the October 22, 2026 new customer value multipliers.
Where: Search, Shopping, Performance Max and Demand Gen campaigns on Google, conversion and catalog ad sets on Meta, and equivalent campaign types on Microsoft Advertising and TikTok.
Why: Conversions differ in worth, and bidding the same amount for a small and a large order wastes budget; value-based bidding shifts spend toward outcomes the advertiser values more, provided the values it receives are accurate.
